 Macau Municipal Affairs Bureau (IAM) warns of excessive patulin in NZ apple juice
 2026-11-19 02:23 
 BY Sherwin Hng 
 Comment:0 
 The Municipal Affairs Bureau (IAM) is urging residents and businesses to stop consuming and selling a batch of bottled apple juice imported from New Zealand after it was found to contain excessive levels of patulin*, a potentially harmful toxin. 
 According to an IAM statement yesterday, the bureau was notified by Hong Kong’s food safety authorities that the product – “100% PURE NZ APPLE JUICE” under the brand “Homegrown” – had been found to contain excessive levels of patulin. 
 The IAM has issued a food alert to local food businesses and deployed officials to inspect retail outlets to prevent the affected product from circulating in the local market. 
 The statement noted that the problematic product is sold in one-litre bottles and has a best-before date of February 11, 2027. Testing found that the sample contained 79 microgrammes of patulin per kilogramme, exceeding the relevant local standards and Macau’s Administrative Regulation No. 13/2016 on maximum levels of mycotoxins in food. 
 Patulin is commonly found in rotten apples and related products. Consuming large amounts may cause nausea, gastrointestinal discomfort, and vomiting, the bureau said. 
 The bureau urged consumers who have purchased the affected batch from local shops and through any other channel, including online shopping and proxy purchasing, to stop drinking it immediately. Businesses possessing the product should also cease supplying and selling it and contact the bureau’s Food Safety Department on 2833 8181. The bureau said it would continue to follow up on the incident to prevent the product from circulating in the market.  
 * Patulin is a mycotoxin (a toxic secondary metabolite produced by fungi) primarily produced by certain species of Penicillium, Aspergillus, and Byssochlamys moulds. It is a major food safety concern, especially in apples and apple products. It is found worldwide in rotting apples, pears, and grapes, and frequently contaminates unpasteurised apple juice, cider, and puree. It is known to be genotoxic (damaging DNA), immunosuppressive, and neurotoxic. – DeepSeek
